deli.title:
Délicorner — a B2B portal,
a design system, and an AI copilot
deli.subtitle: Freelance Product Designer mission at Délicorner (B2B foodtech, ~30 people). Two flagship deliverables in parallel: Corner Digital, the client portal and its design system built from scratch, and CX Copilot, a Slack AI bot that unclogs support and fights churn.
deli.role.value: Freelance Product Designer — DS, UX, AI
deli.mission.title: Two tracks, one standard
deli.mission.p1: Délicorner delivers premium food products in B2B and was running a client-portal MVP with a freelance PM, with no design foundation. I took on two fronts: structuring the product and its design system to make it testable and production-ready, then tackling an operational pain point — CX team overload — with an AI copilot.
deli.mission.p2: Both cases deliberately follow the same arc — Problem → Approach → System → Result — because they answer the same conviction: good design removes friction, whether in the interface or in the process.
deli.case1.title: B2B client portal & design system, from zero to shipped in 2 weeks
deli.case1.sub: A design-to-code pipeline built for speed without sacrificing rigour.
deli.c1.problem.title: The problem
deli.c1.problem.p1: Délicorner had to launch Corner Digital with no design system: a corporate brand guide existed, but no systematised product foundation. The design layer was missing — the one that lets you both test fast with real users and ship developers something reusable, consistent and production-ready.
deli.c1.problem.challenge.label: The challenge:
deli.c1.problem.challenge.text: turning a static brand guide into a living, accessible system that tech can leverage with AI — on a very tight deadline.
deli.c1.approach.title: The approach
deli.c1.approach.intro: Six steps, from token to an AI-ready design system:
deli.c1.s1.d: A DTCG-standard token file derived from the brand guide. A single, scalable source of truth.
deli.c1.s2.d: Pulls components from Storybook into Figma, wired to the same tokens, in 1 click. A free alternative to story.to.design.
deli.c1.s3.d: A genuinely functional high-fidelity proto for testing, built from the PM's MVP.
deli.c1.s4.d: Sessions with 3 clients (Hellowork, NVIDIA, Databricks) to surface friction before industrialisation.
deli.c1.s5.d: Variables, tokens, styles, components — with Claude Code, aligned to the tech stack: Angular, Tailwind, DaisyUI (naming included).
deli.c1.s6.d: DS structured for assisted generation (Figma Make, Claude Code, Codex): the design → dev → AI loop is closed.
deli.c1.system.title: The system
deli.c1.system.p1: The core: a single token propagates to N components, synced in one click across Storybook, code and Figma.
deli.c1.scene.label: Token → Component · 1-click sync
deli.c1.spec.tokens.d: DTCG file derived from the brand guide, single source of truth.
deli.c1.spec.comp.d: Generated and synced via the Storybook→Figma plugin, 1:1 faithful to tokens and variables.
deli.c1.spec.stack.d: Angular + Tailwind + DaisyUI, naming aligned with the existing code.
deli.c1.spec.custom.d: side-panel, calendar, catalog-picker, donut/line/grouped-bar charts — documented (anatomy, slots, do/don't).
deli.c1.spec.ai.d: Structured for assisted generation (Figma Make / Claude Code / Codex).
deli.c1.gallery.title: The portal in pictures
deli.c1.gallery.intro: The functional hi-fi prototype: recurring orders, filterable catalogue, budget tracking and multi-point logistics — from desktop to mobile.
deli.c1.fig.kpi: KPI tracking — budget, cost by country & category
deli.c1.result.title: The result
deli.c1.r1.d: Variables, tokens, styles, components — from the hi-fi mockups.
deli.c1.r2.d: Plus ~102 variables, all connected to the source of truth.
deli.c1.r3.d: Hellowork, NVIDIA, Databricks — friction fixed early.
deli.c1.r4.d: In-house Storybook→Figma plugin, no paid third-party tool.
deli.c1.r.li1: DS reusable by tech with AI — smoother design → dev adoption.
deli.c1.r.li2: Product friction caught before industrialisation thanks to testing.
deli.c1.r.li3: A design-to-code pipeline replayable on the next projects.
deli.case2.title: A Slack AI bot to fight churn and free up the CX teams
deli.case2.sub: Plugged in where the teams already work: centralise, prioritise, accelerate.
deli.c2.problem.title: The problem
deli.c2.problem.p1: CX teams were handling over 100 requests per person per day, scattered across channels (Slack, Front, HubSpot). The result: long response times, customer frustration, churn risk, and CX staff stuck on low-value tasks instead of what matters.
deli.c2.problem.challenge.label: The challenge:
deli.c2.problem.challenge.text: reply fast and well without adding tooling weight — staying inside Slack, where CX already are.
deli.c2.approach.title: The approach
deli.c2.approach.p1: A conversational copilot that analyses each client request, proposes costed resolutions and triggers the right actions — all in a few seconds.
deli.c2.scene.msg: “Coffee machine down for several days, critical SLA missed, no communication during the incident. Solution expected by Friday.”
deli.c2.scene.caption: Animated reconstruction of the real flow: message → analysis → prioritisation → quick actions.
deli.c2.app.li1: Fast, personalised replies to limit frustration and churn.
deli.c2.app.li2: Pragmatic replies, directly usable by the CX rep.
deli.c2.app.li3: One-gesture HubSpot ticket creation, from Slack.
deli.c2.app.li4: Multichannel dashboard: all requests, prioritised, with quick actions.
deli.c2.system.title: The system
deli.c2.spec.if.d: A bot plugged into Slack, where CX already work.
deli.c2.spec.ac.d: One-gesture HubSpot ticket creation, quick actions from the dashboard.
deli.c2.spec.pi.d: A dashboard centralising channels, requests prioritised automatically.
deli.c2.spec.st.d: Vercel + Claude Haiku, aggregating Slack / Front / HubSpot.
deli.c2.fig.analyse: In Slack — analysis, flags & costed proposals
deli.c2.fig.reponse: Validated reply sent to the client in one click
deli.c2.result.title: The result
deli.c2.chart.title: Client response time — before / after
deli.c2.r1.d: Against 5-6 h before (and more ahead of a weekend).
deli.c2.r2.d: +2 to 3 h reallocated to high-value tasks.
deli.c2.r4.d: Lightweight stack (Vercel + Claude Haiku), immediate ROI.
deli.c2.r.li1: Lower response time → less frustration, a direct anti-churn lever.
deli.c2.r.li2: Multichannel centralisation with automatic prioritisation and quick actions.
deli.c2.r.li3: HubSpot ticket opened in one click from Slack.
deli.testimonial.quote: Hugo handled deadlines and delivered quality work in a context of uncertainty and frequent change. He is also highly skilled on AI topics and will bring a lot, both strategically and operationally.
